summary: Describes the PPP Deflate protocol for compressing PPP packets. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: A way to pack the data on a PPP link into a smaller space using the same squeezing trick found in zip and gzip tools.

questions: how to compress ppp packets with deflate
how does ppp deflate handle incompressible data
what is the ppp deflate sequence number
subtitle: Using the zip and gzip deflate format to compress PPP packets, with sequence numbers and a clever escape for incompressible data.

tldr.problem: PPP links need a compression method that is free of encumbrances, cheap on memory and safe for data that does not compress.
tldr.mechanism: Each packet's protocol and data are compressed with the deflate format, prefixed with a 2-byte sequence number, and sent under PPP Protocol 0xFD or 0xFB. Packets that would expand are sent in their original form instead.
tldr.outcome: Receivers that see a sequence gap send a Reset-Request and discard packets until the Reset-Ack arrives. The RFC is Informational and the data shows it has not been obsoleted.

facts.label: Bytes removed from each packet end

today: RFC 1979 is an Informational RFC and the data shows no RFC obsoleting or updating it, so it remains the description of PPP Deflate.

sections.title: Why Deflate
sections.content:
The deflate format, used by PKZIP and gzip and embodied in the zlib library, is the basis here. The RFC lists its features: an apparently unencumbered algorithm with an open specification, a low-overhead escape for incompressible data, heavy use over modem and other point-to-point links, and easy 2:1 compression on the Calgary corpus using less than 64KBytes of memory on both sides.

The format and algorithm are based on Lempel-Ziv LZ77 compression. The RFC includes the zlib copyright notice.
sections.plainLanguage: Zip files already squeeze data well and are free for anyone to use, so PPP borrows the same trick.

sections.title: Deflate Packets in PPP
sections.content:
After PPP reaches the Network-Layer Protocol phase and CCP is Opened, exactly one PPP Deflate datagram goes in the PPP Information field, with Protocol 0xFD or 0xFB. 0xFD is used when multilink is not used or above multilink; 0xFB is used below multilink to compress individual links.

Only packets with PPP Protocol numbers from 0x0000 to 0x3FFF, other than 0xFD and 0xFB, are compressed. Everything else, including control packets, is sent uncompressed because control packets are infrequent and should not be compressed for robustness. If padding is added, the Self-Describing-Padding option must be negotiated first.
sections.plainLanguage: Only ordinary data packets get squeezed. Important control messages are sent as they are, so they are less likely to go wrong.

sections.title: Packet Format
sections.content:
A packet has the PPP Protocol field, a two-byte Sequence number sent most significant octet first, and the data. The sequence number starts at 0 when the dictionary is cleared and goes up by 1 for each packet, including uncompressed ones, wrapping to 0 after 65535.

The data is the compressed Protocol and Data fields of the original packet. Protocol field compression MUST be applied to the original protocol field first, so a protocol number below 0x100 becomes one byte. Each packet must begin at a deflate block boundary and end with a zero-length non-compressed block (BTYPE 00). That makes the last four bytes 0x00 0x00 0xFF 0xFF, and these MUST be removed before transmission; the receiver can reinsert them.
sections.plainLanguage: Every packet gets a number. Each squeezed packet also ends with a fixed little tail, which is cut off for sending and put back by the receiver.

sections.title: Reliability and Resets
sections.content:
PPP Deflate requires in-order delivery. The LCP FCS catches corrupted packets, and the sequence number catches missing or reordered ones. On an unexpected sequence number the receiver SHOULD send a CCP Reset-Request, or MAY force CCP out of Opened with a new Configure-Request, which costs more. The receiver MUST discard compressed packets until a Reset-Ack arrives.

On every Reset-Request the transmitter must clear its compression history and answer with a Reset-Ack, because it cannot know if earlier ones arrived. Both sides reset the sequence number to zero. The receiver need not touch its history on a Reset-Ack because deflate is a sliding-window compressor. Resending requests more often than the link round-trip time causes needless clearing; the RFC suggests waiting, for example, one second, while MUST ensure the transmitter gets at least one.
sections.plainLanguage: If a packet number is missing, the receiver asks the sender to start a fresh page, ignores everything until the sender confirms, and does not nag too often.

sections.title: Handling Incompressible Data
sections.content:
Deflate expands incompressible data by approximately 14-18 bytes, per the RFC's breakdown of deflate worst-case overhead, the end-of-block and synchronization header, the sequence number and the protocol field. To avoid this, a packet that does not fit the link MRU MUST be sent in its original form without CCP encapsulation, and packets with significant expansion that still fit SHOULD be too. The transmitter must still increment the sequence number.

A receiver that gets a packet with a native protocol number in the compressible range assumes it would have expanded and adds it to its compression history. This avoids MTU complications, but both sides must start filling the dictionary with the same packets, and clearing the dictionary must be synchronized with the Configure-Ack or Reset-Ack that starts compression.
sections.plainLanguage: If squeezing a packet would make it bigger, it is sent plain. Both sides still remember it, so they stay in step.

sections.title: The Configuration Option
sections.content: The CCP PPP Deflate option is Type 26 with Length 3 and fields Window, Method, MBZ and Chk. Window is the base-2 logarithm of the LZ77 window size minus 8; decompressors must accept the maximum 32KB window, value 7, and a compressor MUST honor a smaller requested window or reject the option. Method must be binary 1000 (zlib method 8). MBZ must be all zero bits and Chk must be 00, the sequence number check. If peers disagree, no compression is used.
sections.plainLanguage: The two ends agree how big a memory window to use, and the rest of the option is fixed settings.

fields.name: PPP Protocol
fields.desc: 0xFD or 0xFB; may be compressed by Protocol-Field-Compression.

fields.name: Sequence
fields.desc: Wraps after 65535; counts uncompressed packets too.
